title: Adaptive Compliance Intake Router and Scoring Protocol for Multi-Jurisdiction Requests
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem statement: Enterprise customers submit a wide range of security and compliance requests (SOC2 controls, ISO attestation, GDPR/DPA residency questions, HIPAA dataflow concerns, and detailed vendor questionnaires). Current intake is inconsistent: many requests are routed manually, time-to-response varies by team, and the lack of a reproducible scoring model leads to overloaded legal/SE queues and slow sales cycles.

Goal: Implement an adaptive intake router and scoring protocol that classifies incoming compliance asks, assigns a risk/effort score, and routes requests into three deterministic lanes: Self-serve (automated responses + evidence bundle), Concierge (SE + Solutions/Engineering assisted), Legal Review (contract exceptions / full audits). The router should be account-aware (customer tier, hosting mode), jurisdiction-aware (data residency, GDPR/HIPAA triggers), and support manual overrides and audit trails.

Why now: Growing enterprise pipeline for Dedicated/Private deployments with stricter SLAs has increased security intake traffic by ~55% YoY. We need a repeatable, measurable triage flow to reduce mean time to first response and surface high-risk items earlier.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Incoming questionnaire submissions are scored and routed automatically 80% of the time with audit logs.
2) Self-serve lane supports templated evidence bundles for top 10 enterprise asks.
3) Concierge lane SLA: initial human response <48 hours for priority enterprise accounts.
4) Legal Review lane creates templated issue with required artifacts and intake fields.
5) Dashboard shows queue sizes, mean time to response, and accuracy of classification (target >= 85% precision for Legal lane).
success_metrics:
- Mean time to first response reduced from 7 days to <=48 hours for enterprise accounts.
- % of fully automated responses for low-risk asks >=40%.
- Reduction in legal queue growth rate by 30% within 8 weeks.
- Customer satisfaction survey NPS for security requests >= +30 on closed interactions.
proposed_design_summary:
1) Frontline intake: single web form + email ingestion + CSV questionnaire upload.
2) Signal extraction: automated parser extracts keywords, control IDs (e.g., SOC2 CC1-CC8), jurisdiction flags, hosting mode, requested artifacts.
3) Scoring engine: weighted factors (customer_tier: 30%, data_sensitivity: 25%, compliance_scope: 20%, hosting_mode: 15%, historical_escalations: 10%). Score thresholds map to lanes.
4) Routing & automation: integrate with internal Evidence Bundler service to assemble artifacts and with Zendesk/GitHub to create tickets in the right queue.
5) Escalation: automatic escalation to Legal + PM when scores exceed a hard threshold or when manual flags are set.
6) Observability: events emitted (intake.received, intake.scored, intake.routed, intake.escalated) and per-account dashboards in Console.
detailed_scoring_example:
Example weights and thresholds (prototype):
- customer_tier: enterprise=30, midmarket=15, self-serve=0
- data_sensitivity: pii=25, health=25, none=0
- compliance_scope: contract/DPA=20, audit=20, questionnaire=10
- hosting_mode: private/VPC=15, dedicated=10, hosted=0
- historical_escalations: yes=10, no=0

Score buckets: 0-24 -> Self-serve; 25-59 -> Concierge; 60+ -> Legal Review.
Note: thresholds and weights are tunable and will be refined during the pilot with a labeled dataset of 400 historical requests.
tradeoffs_and_considerations:
- Strict automation reduces human overhead but risks misclassifying nuanced legal exceptions.
- Heavier weighting on customer tier favors enterprise accounts; must avoid starving smaller customers.
- Triage latency vs. thoroughness: parsing and scoring needs to be fast (<2s for typical intake) to support synchronous responses.
- GDPR/HIPAA-specific flows require additional metadata capture and legal-approved copy in self-serve responses.
- Privacy: parsed PII must not be stored in plain text in the scoring service; use tokenization/encryption and limited retention.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (4 weeks): intake form + basic parser + scoring prototype + manual routing integration.
Phase 2 (6 weeks): evidence bundler integration + automated self-serve templates + dashboards.
Phase 3 (4 weeks): legal templates, SLA automation, manual override UX, pilot with 5 enterprise accounts.
Phase 4 (ongoing): model tuning, metrics review, expand to other request channels (sales email, partner portal).
risks:
- Inaccurate parser for vendor questionnaires with custom formats.
- Underreporting of jurisdictional flags leading to compliance exposure.
- Resource constraints for building evidence bundle connectors to third-party storage.
- Change management: sales/SE adoption of new intake process might be slow.
mitigations:
- Start with a limited schema for top 20 questionnaire formats and build iterative parsers.
- Introduce mandatory jurisdiction question during intake when ambiguity detected.
- Prioritize connectors (S3, GCS, Confluence) and fallback manual upload.
- Run training and internal comms; include SE owners as pilot partners.
